source: /feedback review + /iterate (2026-08-10) — surfaced while correcting the azure/ 'schema/data' mislabel
title: Make the Azure SQL seed rows reproducible from the repo (azure/ is DDL-only)
description: The spec states in three places that /azure/ holds DDL only — procurement.sql and supplier_info.sql each contain one CREATE TABLE and zero INSERT statements (§ Data Architecture Setup Scripts, § Expected Data Profiles L1136, § Testing Strategy L1327). Those statements are accurate; the gap they describe is real. The synthetic rows backing fact_procurement were seeded by hand outside the repo, so a clean rebuild of the Azure SQL source is impossible from a fresh clone and the row counts in § Expected Data Profiles can only be re-derived by measuring the live lakehouse. Close the gap by committing a reproducible seed alongside the DDL: either exported INSERT statements or a deterministic generator with a pinned seed. IMPORTANT — do NOT export from the laptop. The erik-laptop firewall rule (37.247.31.201/32) was deliberately deleted from the procurement-supplier Azure SQL server on 2026-08-01 (FB-009, commit c0fcb3a) once the pipeline moved to the Fabric Connection oem_azuresql_procurement; re-adding it to run a local export would reopen the security loose end that cleanup closed. Run the export from a Fabric notebook over the existing connection instead, which executes in the Fabric runtime and needs no firewall change. Note the two tables differ in character: supplier_info is reference data (small, stable, a literal INSERT dump is fine) while procurement is transactional volume (a generator may be the better fit). Decide per-table rather than forcing one approach on both.
acceptanceCriteria: A fresh clone can populate both Azure SQL tables from repo contents alone — no hand-seeding, no out-of-band file — using the committed DDL plus the new seed artifact.
The seed reproduces row counts and distributions consistent with the figures in § Expected Data Profiles; any deliberate divergence is stated in the task notes.
No Azure SQL firewall rule is added for a laptop IP — the export or generation path runs in the Fabric runtime over the oem_azuresql_procurement connection (or is a pure offline generator).
If a generator is used, it is deterministic — a pinned seed produces identical output across runs.
The three spec statements that currently say the rows are 'not reproducible from the repo' are updated to match the new reality (routes through /iterate per DEC-016).
No credentials are committed — the seed artifact contains data only, and connection details stay in the Fabric connection or secure/ (gitignored).
notes: Requested by Erik 2026-08-10 (out-of-spec gate — the spec documents the gap as current state but nowhere requires reproducibility, so this is new scope rather than a correction). Surfaced during the /feedback review + /iterate pass that relabelled azure/ from 'schema/data' to 'schema (DDL only)'; the relabel made the record honest, this task closes the underlying gap. owner=both: Claude authors the export notebook or generator locally, Erik runs it in the Fabric UI and confirms the round trip, per the project's Fabric-UI/local-code split. The AC5 spec edit routes through /iterate, not a direct write. CONFIRMED by Erik 2026-08-11 ('confirm') - Claude's half is cleared to start. [IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11] Both tables seeded by literal INSERT dump (132 procurement rows, 11 supplier rows) rather than a generator -- procurement measured at only 132 rows, so exact beats plausible and AC4's determinism requirement is not triggered (stated, not skipped; export run twice, byte-identical). Rows read from the LAKEHOUSE bronze copies over OneLake DFS (Delta v101/v99), never from Azure SQL -- no firewall rule added or requested, FB-009 loose end stays closed (AC3). Verified by executing DDL+seed against in-memory SQLite: both parse, land 132/11 rows, and compare EQUAL to the exported source parquet on every column. Distribution checks pass (kg=108/pcs=24, 11 distinct materials and suppliers, full referential integrity, 12 raw dates transposing to 2024 month-ends). Credential scan clean with a positive control hitting secure/user_creation.sql (AC6); secure/ confirmed gitignored. One deliberate AC2 divergence: UnitPriceEUR written at 2dp to match DECIMAL(18,2) while the live column is float32 -- all 132 values verified as the exact float32 image of their 2dp value, so a rebuild is identical to the cent. SCOPE ADDITION (DEC-015 coupled sub-decision): the DDL created dbo.Procurement/dbo.SupplierInfo, names NO ingestion artifact has ever read -- corrected to dbo.procurement_transactional/dbo.supplier_ref, proven long-standing by the retired dataflow's mashup.pq reading the same corrected names. *** HAZARD: the pre-existing DROP in each DDL now targets the LIVE table instead of a non-existent one -- running the DDL alone destroys live source data. Mitigated by running DDL+seed as one script and by the data now being repo-recoverable, but Erik must accept this consciously. *** AC5's three spec statements are drafted, NOT applied (DEC-016). [VERIFICATION FAIL #1: they were asserted parked but were NOT actually written; remediated same day as merge-queue MQ-002.] Friction: FR-073, FR-074. NOT committed, NOT pushed. [ATTEMPT 2 2026-08-11] Remediation was orchestrator-only -- the deliverables themselves passed 8 of 9 probes and were not touched. MQ-002 appended to .claude/support/reference/merge-queue.md with all three verbatim targets, honouring the verifier's distinction that the § Setup Scripts target is an ADDITION (the 'DDL only' description remains literally true) rather than a correction. DEC-015 and these notes corrected to stop asserting a merge-queue state that did not exist.

verification_history.notes: FAIL attempt 1 on ONE narrow gap; 8 of 9 probes passed, several emphatically. DROP escalation ADJUDICATED and mitigations HOLD: the DROP was pre-existing (visible on the diff's '-' lines), only its target moved; both seeds verified to open with DELETE and close with a row-count THROW (50001/50002), idempotent on re-run; the DESTRUCTIVE banner is in all four file headers where a runner sees it; and the Copy source is a bare full-table dataset with no query/filter, so the 132/11 rows ARE the complete source and a rebuild restores every value. Table-name correction JUSTIFIED on evidence the verifier read itself: the retired mashup.pq (L10/L14/L32) and the live pipeline-content.json (L529-530, L596-597) both read the corrected names. AC1 re-run independently in SQLite -> exactly 132/11, with T-SQL fidelity checked (string widths, 2dp precision, 1000-row VALUES limit, quoting, date validity). AC2 spot-checked on real values: all 132 prices exactly 2dp, no two distinct 2dp values share a float32 image, round(float32(v),2)==v throughout; kg=108/pcs=24 corroborated against task-030's independent 2026-07-23 live measurement. AC3 PASS. AC4's 'not triggered' reading is LEGITIMATE -- the criterion is explicitly conditional on a generator being used. AC6 PASS with positive control. Transposed dates PASS -- all 12 in RAW form, zero beginning '2024-', so nothing double-corrects (this one would have been silent and catastrophic). THE FAILURE: AC5's drafted spec text was asserted parked in the merge queue but was never written there -- an orchestrator hand-off gap, not implementer negligence. Remediated same day as MQ-002, including the verifier's distinction that the § Setup Scripts target needs an ADDITION (the DDL-only description is still literally true) rather than a correction.

test_protocol.summary: Rebuild both Azure SQL source tables from the repo in the Fabric runtime, then confirm the pipeline still ingests them. Two pre-flight gates must clear before any script runs -- step 3 onward is DESTRUCTIVE.
test_protocol.automated_results: Local verification complete and passed: DDL+seed executed in SQLite land exactly 132/11 rows and compare EQUAL to the exported source parquet on every column; T-SQL fidelity checked (string widths, 2dp precision, 1000-row VALUES limit, quoting, date validity); distributions pass (kg=108/pcs=24, 11 distinct materials and suppliers, full referential integrity, all 12 dates in RAW transposed form). What remains is Fabric-runtime execution over the live connection.

steps.instruction: PRE-FLIGHT GATE 1 (destructive-action acceptance). Read the DESTRUCTIVE banner atop azure/procurement.sql and azure/supplier_info.sql, and the '! Consequence' table in DEC-015. The DROP was always there, but it now names the LIVE table the pipeline reads -- running a DDL WITHOUT its seed destroys the live source data. Accept consciously or halt.
steps.expected: You accept the hazard knowing the data is now fully recoverable from the repo, and commit to running each DDL together with its seed as ONE script.

steps.instruction: PRE-FLIGHT GATE 2 (write permission). The oem_azuresql_procurement connection has only ever needed SELECT, and secure/grant_permissions.sql grants INSERT on the OLD names only. Confirm the principal holds INSERT on dbo.procurement_transactional and dbo.supplier_ref; issue the GRANTs first if not.
steps.expected: Principal has INSERT on both corrected names. A permissions failure at step 3 points here, not at the seed.

steps.instruction: In the Fabric runtime over the oem_azuresql_procurement connection, run azure/procurement.sql immediately followed by azure/procurement_seed.sql as a SINGLE script.
steps.expected: Completes with no error; the closing row-count guard does not THROW 50002.

steps.instruction: Same way: azure/supplier_info.sql immediately followed by azure/supplier_info_seed.sql as a SINGLE script.
steps.expected: Completes with no error; the guard does not THROW 50001.

steps.instruction: Query the rebuilt tables: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dbo.procurement_transactional; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dbo.supplier_ref;
steps.expected: Exactly 132 and 11. UnitPriceEUR now reads as clean 2-decimal values instead of float32 noise -- the one deliberate, documented divergence, identical to the cent.

steps.instruction: Idempotency check: re-run each seed alone and re-count.
steps.expected: Still 132 and 11 -- each seed opens with a DELETE, so a repeat run neither doubles rows nor trips the guard.

steps.instruction: Run the bronze Copy activities (bronze_copy_procurement_transactional, bronze_copy_supplier_ref) and check the bronze tables.
steps.expected: Bronze lands 132 and 11 rows from the rebuilt source; silver dates land in calendar 2024 and downstream gold is unchanged from the pre-rebuild state.
